## Problem

Life Saving Victoria's Operational Service Summary tool lives as a claude.ai artifact: one 130 KB vanilla-JS `index.html` whose storage is claude.ai's artifact store and whose "capabilities" (`window.claude.use("user" | "downloads" | "sample")`) only exist inside claude.ai. That host cannot reach the Bureau of Meteorology, so twice a week a member runs a bookmarklet on bom.gov.au and pastes the result into the Weather tab by hand. The data is behind claude.ai sharing rather than an organisational login, the page cannot be slotted into LIMSOC's interface chooser, and nothing is automated. The tool needs a real home: an authenticated site at a stable URL, a multi-user backend with live updates, and a scheduled job that fills the weather grid without anyone pasting anything.

## Vision

A comms member opens nicholas.wood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary on Tuesday morning, signs in exactly the way they would for AccessBuddy, sees "Welcome Sarah" on a LIMSOC-styled chooser, clicks Service Management, and the Weather tab already holds seven days of BOM figures issued at 05:30 that morning. A colleague editing SC40's hours in another browser appears live. The Word export fills LSV's own template. Nothing about the app itself feels different from the artifact; what changed is that it is now a service rather than a page.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the app's UI, flows, wording, or document generation beyond what hosting, auth, storage, and weather automation strictly require. The Excel-like simplicity is deliberate.
- Any call to LIMSOC production (limsoc.com.au), for reads or writes, and any new LIMSOC API integration without Nick's explicit approval. Unit data came from staging only.
- Public republication of BOM data. The site stays behind login; no anonymous weather endpoint.
- Paid infrastructure beyond Google Cloud's free tier unless Nick approves it after a cost estimate.
- A second interface-chooser entry, LIMSOC embedding, or SSO with LIMSOC. The chooser keeps the look so it can be slotted in later; the slotting is not this work.
- Mobile app, offline mode, or PWA packaging.
- Rebuilding the page in a framework. Splitting into modules is allowed only with behaviour held identical.

## Principles

- **Same security posture as AccessBuddy, not a lookalike.** Sign-in, session handling, and access checks are the same mechanisms, ideally the same code, so one audit covers both.
- **A member's typed value is sacred.** Automation fills gaps and refreshes its own figures; it never overwrites a human edit.
- **Nothing readable without a session.** Page, data API, and live-update channel all refuse signed-out requests.
- **Infrastructure as code, deploy from a release.** If it is not in Terraform or a workflow, it does not exist.
- **Cost honesty.** Anything outside the free tier is surfaced with an estimate before it is created.
- **Behaviour parity is the regression test.** The artifact is the oracle: exports, imports, and views must match it byte-for-intent.

## Constraints

- Auth: Firebase Auth email magic link, email OTP, and passkeys as in AccessBuddy (`apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts`), producing the `session` cookie (httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days), validated server-side on every request. No passwords. Dev login only when `NODE_ENV !== production`.
- Hosting: Next.js on Cloud Run, australia-southeast1, Terraform in `infra/terraform`, GitHub Actions CI, release-please gated deploy over Workload Identity Federation, Secret Manager for secrets, Cloud Scheduler for the weather job authenticated with a cron secret header.
- URL: served under the path prefix `/lsv/dailysummary`; the page keeps hash routing (`#home`, `#services`, `#weather`, `#events`, `#report`, `#setup`).
- Storage interface preserved verbatim: `db.collection(name).onSnapshot(cb)` → `{docs:[{id,data()}]}`; `db.doc(path).onSnapshot(cb)` → `{exists,data()}`; `db.doc(path).set(obj)`; `db.doc(path).delete()`. Collections `units`, `events`, `weather`, `confirmations`, `summaries`; docs `config/settings`, `config/contacts`.
- Weather feeds via anonymous FTP only: `ftp://ftp.bom.gov.au/anon/gen/fwo/IDV10753.xml`, `IDV10752.xml`, `IDV10751.xml`, with a descriptive User-Agent. Not the www.bom.gov.au/fwo URLs.
- Wording: "members" never "staff". `unit.area` holds Region (Central/East/West); `unit.regionName` holds Area (Bass, Port Phillip, Kingston, ...).
- Build: changes go into `src/ux/*` parts and `build.py` rebuilds `index.html`; never hand-edit the built file. Library versions pinned: docx@8.5.0, xlsx@0.18.5, jszip@3.10.1.
- Tooling: bun, TypeScript, Terraform; Python only where the pack already uses it (`build.py`, `build_seed.py`).

## Goal

The Operational Service Summary runs at `https://nicholas.wood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary` on Nick's Google Cloud with AccessBuddy's sign-in, session, and access model; its data lives in an authenticated backend seeded from the 2026-11-16 export with live multi-user updates; a twice-daily Cloud Scheduler job fills seven days of BOM weather without overwriting member-typed values; and a README covers deploy, rollback, weather rerun, and restore.

OBSERVE is complete as far as it can go. I did everything that does not depend on the pack, and it surfaced four decisions that are yours, plus one blocker.

**What I found about AccessBuddy** (surveyed the repo at `projects/accessbuddy/code`):
- Sign-in is Firebase Auth email magic link, email OTP, and passkeys, sent via Resend. Sessions are a 14-day httpOnly `session` cookie checked per route by `getAuthUser()`. No passwords. Rate limits live in Postgres.
- Hosting is Next.js 15 on one Cloud Run service in australia-southeast1, Terraform, GitHub Actions with WIF, deploy only when release-please cuts a release, Cloud Scheduler with a cron secret header, Cloud Run domain mapping plus Cloud DNS.
- It does not use Firestore. Data is Postgres on a Cloud SQL db-f1-micro instance, which is the one paid piece of its stack. There is no CSP or any security header.

**BOM test result:** the FTP fetch of IDV10753.xml from Cloud Run in australia-southeast1 works. One-off job `bom-probe` in accessbuddy-dev returned FTP code 226 with the full 424 KB file in under a second. The weather job is viable as specified.

**Decisions I need from you before building** (recommendation first):

1. **Backend.** AccessBuddy's Postgres does not map to the page's `db.collection().onSnapshot()` interface, and Firestore does. My recommendation is Firestore in Native mode in a new GCP project, with the AccessBuddy sign-in flow and session cookie unchanged and Firestore security rules gated on a member allow-list. It is free, gives live updates natively, and needs no instance. The faithful alternative is a new database on the existing AccessBuddy Cloud SQL instance at zero marginal cost, with live updates over SSE from Cloud Run, but it puts LSV data inside the AccessBuddy project and VPC. A new Cloud SQL instance would cost roughly AU$15 to 20 a month and I do not recommend it.
2. **Domain.** nicholas.wood.com.au does not exist and neither does wood.com.au. nicholaswood.com.au is registered at GoDaddy and parked. Did you mean nicholaswood.com.au, and may I point it at Cloud Run via Cloud DNS as AccessBuddy does?
3. **Libraries and CSP.** AccessBuddy has no CSP, so your literal instruction says keep the CDN tags. I recommend vendoring the three libraries and adding a strict CSP anyway since this is a fresh app. Your call.
4. **GCP project.** New project for this app on your existing billing account, or inside accessbuddy-prod? New project is my recommendation unless you pick the shared Cloud SQL option.

**Cost estimate for the recommended shape:** Cloud Run at min 0, Firestore, two Scheduler jobs, five secrets, Artifact Registry and Firebase Auth all sit inside free tiers. A Cloud DNS zone for the domain is about US$0.20 a month. Expect under AU$1 a month.

Nick picked Firestore, nicholaswood.com.au, a new GCP project, and dropped the pack. First a plain answer on CSP, then I'll locate the pack and continue into THINK.

A CSP, Content Security Policy, is a response header the server sends with the page that tells the browser which origins it may load scripts, styles, and data from. With one in place, a script injected into the page from anywhere not on the list simply does not run, which blunts cross-site scripting. AccessBuddy does not set one. If I keep the three CDN tags I would have to allow cdn.jsdelivr.net in the policy, which means trusting that CDN forever. Vendoring the three files into the app lets the policy say "this site only". I will vendor and set a strict CSP as the default since it is cheap and reversible. Say so if you would rather keep the CDN tags.

## Usage Modes

1. **Standalone** — Search, present findings, say: "Context loaded on [topic]. Most recent session: [X]. What would you like to do?"
2. **Paired with request** — Search first, then execute the request informed by context.

Run all four searches simultaneously in a single response:

**1A. Session Registry**
Read `~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/STATE/work.json`. Match entries where `task`, slug (object key), or `sessionName` contains "paired: accessbuddy firebase auth magic link cloud run domain mapping workload identity federation release-please deploy gotchas" (case-insensitive). Extract: task, phase, progress, effort. Limit to **5 most recent** matches.

**1B. Session Names**

Only if Phase 1 returned fewer than 3 total matches, run in parallel:


**2B. Current Project Git History**


## After Search: Load ISA Summaries (NOT full ISAs)

From Phase 1C/1D matches, identify the **3 most recent ISAs** (by directory date prefix). Read only the **first 10 lines** of each (title + summary). Do NOT read full ISAs — the main agent can request a full read if needed.

Compact single list. Omit sections with no results. **Keep total output under 40 lines.**

```
═══ CONTEXT: paired: accessbuddy firebase auth magic link cloud run domain mapping workload identity federation release-please deploy gotchas ═══════════════════════
```

# FirstPrinciples Skill

Foundational reasoning methodology based on Elon Musk's physics-based thinking framework. Deconstructs problems to fundamental truths rather than reasoning by analogy.

## Core Concept

**Reasoning by Analogy** (default, often wrong):
- "How did we solve something similar?"
- "What do others do?"
- Copies existing solutions with slight variations

**Reasoning from First Principles** (this skill):
- "What are the fundamental truths here?"
- "What is this actually made of?"
- Rebuilds solutions from irreducible facts

## When to Use

- **Architects**: Challenge "is this actually a constraint or just how we've always done it?"
- **Pentesters**: Identify actual attack surfaces vs. assumed security boundaries
- **RedTeam**: Sharpen adversarial analysis by deconstructing assumptions
- **Engineers**: When stuck, rebuild from fundamentals
- **Any skill**: When inherited assumptions may be limiting the solution space


## Workflow Routing

Route to the appropriate workflow based on the request.

**When executing a workflow, output this notification directly:**

```
Running the **WorkflowName** workflow in the **FirstPrinciples** skill to ACTION...
```

  - Break problem into fundamental parts → `Workflows/Deconstruct.md`
  - Challenge assumptions systematically → `Workflows/Challenge.md`
  - Rebuild solution from fundamentals → `Workflows/Reconstruct.md`

## The 3-Step Framework

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  STEP 1: DECONSTRUCT                                    │
│  "What is this really made of?"                         │
│  Break down to constituent parts and fundamental truths │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  STEP 2: CHALLENGE                                      │
│  "Is this a real constraint or an assumption?"          │
│  Classify each element as hard/soft constraint          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                          ↓
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  STEP 3: RECONSTRUCT                                    │
│  "Given only the truths, what's optimal?"               │
│  Build new solution from fundamentals, ignoring form    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Key Questions

### Deconstruction Questions
- What is this actually made of?
- What are the constituent parts?
- What is the actual cost/value of each part?
- What would a physicist say about this?

### Challenge Questions
- Is this a hard constraint (physics/reality) or soft constraint (policy/choice)?
- What if we removed this constraint entirely?
- Who decided this was a constraint and why?
- What evidence supports this assumption?

### Reconstruction Questions
- If we started from scratch with only the fundamental truths, what would we build?
- What field has solved an analogous problem differently?
- Are we optimizing function or form?
- What's the simplest solution that satisfies only the hard constraints?

## Constraint Classification

When analyzing any system, classify constraints:

| Type | Definition | Example | Can Change? |
|------|------------|---------|-------------|
| **Hard** | Physics/reality | "Data can't travel faster than light" | No |
| **Soft** | Policy/choice | "We always use REST APIs" | Yes |
| **Assumption** | Unvalidated belief | "Users won't accept that UX" | Maybe false |

**Rule**: Only hard constraints are truly immutable. Soft constraints and assumptions should be challenged.

## Integration Pattern

Other skills invoke FirstPrinciples like this:

```markdown
## Before Analysis
→ Use FirstPrinciples/Challenge on all stated constraints
→ Classify each as hard/soft/assumption

## When Stuck
→ Use FirstPrinciples/Deconstruct to break down the problem
→ Use FirstPrinciples/Reconstruct to rebuild from fundamentals

## For Adversarial Analysis
→ RedTeam uses FirstPrinciples/Challenge to attack assumptions
→ Pentester uses FirstPrinciples/Deconstruct on security model
```

## Examples

### Example 1: Architecture Decision
**Problem**: "We need microservices because that's how modern apps are built"

**First Principles Analysis**:
1. **Deconstruct**: What does this app actually need? (team size, scale, complexity)
2. **Challenge**: Is "microservices" a hard constraint? No - it's reasoning by analogy
3. **Reconstruct**: Given our 3-person team and moderate scale, a modular monolith optimizes for our actual constraints

### Example 2: Security Assessment
**Problem**: "The firewall protects the internal network"

**First Principles Analysis**:
1. **Deconstruct**: What is the firewall actually doing? (packet filtering on specific ports)
2. **Challenge**: Does packet filtering = protection? What about authorized ports? Insider threats?
3. **Reconstruct**: Protection requires defense in depth - firewall is one layer, not "the" protection

### Example 3: Cost Optimization
**Problem**: "Cloud hosting costs gates,000/month - that's just what it costs"

**First Principles Analysis**:
1. **Deconstruct**: What are we actually paying for? (compute, storage, bandwidth, managed services)
2. **Challenge**: Is managed Kubernetes a hard requirement? Is this region required?
3. **Reconstruct**: Actual compute needs = the,000. The other the,000 is convenience we're choosing to pay for

## Output Format

When using FirstPrinciples, output should include:

```markdown
## First Principles Analysis: [Topic]

### Deconstruction
- **Constituent Parts**: [List fundamental elements]
- **Actual Values**: [Real costs/metrics, not market prices]

### Constraint Classification
| Constraint | Type | Evidence | Challenge |
|------------|------|----------|-----------|
| [X] | Hard/Soft/Assumption | [Why] | [What if removed?] |

### Reconstruction
- **Fundamental Truths**: [Only the hard constraints]
- **Optimal Solution**: [Built from fundamentals]
- **Form vs Function**: [Are we optimizing the right thing?]

### Key Insight
[One sentence: what assumption was limiting us?]
```

## Principles

1. **Physics First** - Real constraints come from physics/reality, not convention
2. **Function Over Form** - Optimize what you're trying to accomplish, not how it's traditionally done
3. **Question Everything** - Every assumption is guilty until proven innocent
4. **Cross-Domain Synthesis** - Solutions from unrelated fields often apply
5. **Rebuild, Don't Patch** - When assumptions are wrong, start fresh rather than fixing

## Anti-Patterns to Avoid

- **Reasoning by Analogy**: "Company X does it this way, so should we"
- **Accepting Market Prices**: "Batteries cost $600/kWh" without checking material costs
- **Form Fixation**: Improving the suitcase instead of inventing wheels
- **Soft Constraint Worship**: Treating policies as physics
- **Premature Optimization**: Optimizing before understanding fundamentals

---

**Attribution**: Framework derived from Elon Musk's first principles methodology as documented by James Clear, Mayo Oshin, and public interviews.

## Gotchas

- **Decompose to AXIOMS — fundamental truths, not just simpler components.** The value is in finding the irreducible elements.
- **Challenge INHERITED assumptions specifically.** What does everyone assume that might be wrong?
- **This is analysis/reasoning, not implementation.** "Analyze" = FirstPrinciples. "Fix" = do the work directly.

## Execution Log

After completing any workflow, append a single JSONL entry:

```bash
echo '{"ts":"'$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)'","skill":"FirstPrinciples","workflow":"WORKFLOW_USED","input":"8_WORD_SUMMARY","status":"ok|error","duration_s":SECONDS}' >> ~/.claude/PAI/MEMORY/SKILLS/execution.jsonl
```

Replace `WORKFLOW_USED` with the workflow executed, `8_WORD_SUMMARY` with a brief input description, and `SECONDS` with approximate wall-clock time. Log `status: "error"` if the workflow failed.

## First Principles Analysis: access control for the OSS data layer

**Deconstruction.** The system is five parts: proof of identity (Firebase Auth), a membership decision (is this email allowed), transport of that decision to the data boundary, live propagation of writes, and gating of the page itself. AccessBuddy fuses the first three at each route via `getAuthUser()` plus a membership row.

| Constraint | Type | Evidence | Challenge |
|---|---|---|---|
| Same sign-in UX as AccessBuddy | Soft, user-mandated | Firebase Auth email link and OTP exist in both designs | Holds either way |
| Nothing readable without login | Hard | Nick's done-condition 1 | Both designs satisfy if rules deny unauthenticated |
| Live multi-user updates | Hard | done-condition 2 | SSE through Cloud Run bills CPU per open stream; browser SDK offloads it to Firestore free |
| Free tier | Soft, stated | Nick's cost rule | SSE proxy risks it under long-open tabs; SDK does not |
| OTP path has no browser Firebase session | Assumption | AccessBuddy OTP mints an HMAC cookie only | Server can mint a Firebase custom token for any session holder |

**Reconstruction.** The irreducible primitive is a verifiable assertion "this request is from an allow-listed member" evaluated at the data boundary. With Firestore the data boundary is the rules engine, so the assertion must ride in the Firebase ID token. The clean way: after the session cookie is validated and the allow-list checked server-side (exactly where AccessBuddy does it), the server mints a Firebase custom token carrying a `member: true` claim. The page exchanges it with `signInWithCustomToken`, and rules require `request.auth.token.member == true` for every read and write, plus shape checks (known collections, `updatedBy == request.auth.uid`). Membership enforcement stays in Node like AccessBuddy; rules are a second lock, not the policy. Removal from the allow-list calls `revokeRefreshTokens`, so revocation works for all three sign-in paths.

**Key insight.** The session cookie and the Firestore token are the same identity from the same provider, so I do not need two auth schemes, only one mint step behind the existing cookie.

## Core Concept

Instead of analyzing a problem once, run 2-8 structured passes through the same problem, each from a systematically different **lens**. Each pass surfaces requirements, edge cases, and criteria invisible from other angles. The combination yields ISC criteria that no single-pass analysis could produce.

## Use / Win

**When to use:** Any time you have time budget beyond Standard tier and the task is important enough that getting the ISC right matters more than speed. This is the single most valuable thinking capability for the OBSERVE phase. If you're at Extended effort or above, you should be asking "why NOT use IterativeDepth?" rather than "why use it?"

Concrete triggers:
- **Extra time available** — Extended+ effort means you have the budget. Spend it on understanding the problem deeply before writing ISC, not on writing more code faster.
- **Deep analysis of what's actually being asked** — The user said X. But what do they actually need? What are they trying to accomplish? What would make them rate this 9-10? Single-pass reverse engineering catches the obvious. IterativeDepth catches the rest.
- **Different angles of approach** — Before committing to an approach, explore the problem from stakeholder, failure, temporal, experiential, and constraint-inversion angles. The right approach often only becomes obvious after seeing the problem from 3-4 directions.
- **Important or critical tasks** — When the user says "this is critical" or the task has high blast radius, the cost of missing a dimension is much higher than the cost of 2-5 extra minutes of analysis.
- **Tasks you've never done before** — Novel work has the highest density of hidden requirements. IterativeDepth is insurance against the things you don't know you don't know.

**What you win:**
- **ISC criteria that single-pass analysis cannot produce.** Each lens surfaces requirements invisible from other angles. A 4-lens pass routinely discovers 30-50% more criteria than direct analysis.

- **Approach clarity.** Seeing the problem from failure, stakeholder, and constraint-inversion angles often reveals that the obvious approach is wrong and a better path exists.
- **Confidence.** When ISC criteria are built on multi-angle analysis, you can execute with conviction instead of discovering gaps halfway through.

**The default mental model should be:** At Extended+ effort, IterativeDepth is not optional enrichment — it's the standard way to understand what you're building before you build it.

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AccessBuddy — Production Deployment
# Called by release-please workflow when a release is created.
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

name: Deploy

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  GCP_REGION: australia-southeast1
  CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE: accessbuddy-production
  AR_REPO: accessbuddy
  IMAGE_NAME: app

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

# Required for Workload Identity Federation
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Cloud Run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ci]

    environment: production

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        id: auth
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - name: Setup Google Cloud SDK
        uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - name: Configure Docker for Artifact Registry
        run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

      - name: Build Docker image
        env:
          IMAGE_TAG: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN }} \
            -t ${IMAGE_TAG}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE_TAG}:v${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE_TAG}:latest \
            .

      - name: Push Docker image
        env:
          IMAGE_TAG: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker push ${IMAGE_TAG}:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ${IMAGE_TAG}:v${{ inputs.version }}
          docker push ${IMAGE_TAG}:latest

      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} \
            --image=${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} \
            --project=${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

FROM oven/bun:1.3 AS base

# Install dependencies
FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock turbo.json ./
COPY apps/web/package.json ./apps/web/
COPY packages/shared/package.json ./packages/shared/
COPY packages/db/package.json ./packages/db/
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

# Build the application
FROM base AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=deps /app/apps/web/node_modules ./apps/web/node_modules
COPY --from=deps /app/packages/shared/node_modules ./packages/shared/node_modules
COPY --from=deps /app/packages/db/node_modules ./packages/db/node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# NEXT_PUBLIC_* vars must be present at build time — Next.js inlines them
# into the client bundle. Pass via --build-arg at docker build time.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN

# Build shared and db packages first, then web
RUN cd packages/shared && bun run build || true
RUN cd packages/db && bun run build || true
RUN cd apps/web && bun run build

# Production image
FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

RUN groupadd --system --gid 1001 nodejs
RUN useradd --system --uid 1001 --gid nodejs nextjs

# Copy standalone Next.js output
COPY --from=builder /app/apps/web/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder /app/apps/web/.next/static ./apps/web/.next/static
COPY --from=builder /app/apps/web/public ./apps/web/public

# Copy DB package for migrations and seed
COPY --from=builder /app/packages/db ./packages/db
COPY --from=builder /app/packages/shared ./packages/shared
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/scripts ./scripts

# Entrypoint script
COPY --from=builder /app/scripts/entrypoint.sh /app/entrypoint.sh
RUN chmod +x /app/entrypoint.sh

EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME="0.0.0.0"

CMD ["sh", "/app/entrypoint.sh"]

🎲 RISKIEST ASSUMPTIONS: the page's inline script can be served under a strict CSP without a rewrite (artifact likely has one large inline block); AccessBuddy's auth modules port cleanly without Postgres (rate limits and OTP store need a Firestore backing); GoDaddy nameserver change and domain verification are Nick-side actions that gate the custom domain.
⚰️ PREMORTEM: weather job silently stops and nobody notices; custom-token endpoint abused; BOM XML parsed with DTDs enabled; "next 7 days" computed in UTC and the Melbourne date slips; deploy race on release-please leaves a release with nothing deployed; Firebase web key unrestricted.
☑️ PREREQUISITES CHECK: pack still missing; gh token invalid on Mac and gh absent on Linux, so repo creation and CI need Nick's `gh auth login`; Firebase CLI absent, so I will use the REST API with a gcloud token; codex CLI status on Mac unknown.

🎯 EUPHORIC SURPRISE PREDICTION: 8/10 — one server-minted Firebase token behind the AccessBuddy cookie gives live Firestore for free with a single identity, and a weather status line in the tab tells members when BOM last ran.

━━━ 📋 PLAN ━━━ 3/7

📐 PLANNING:
 📐 SCOPE: breadth-then-depth — stand up project, auth, data, weather, infra in parallel
 📐 SESSION: single
 📐 ROOT-CAUSE: n/a, greenfield deployment

📦 DELIVERABLE MANIFEST:
 📦 D1: "same security measures and login procedures as accessbuddy" at /lsv/dailysummary
 📦 D2: "Replace the claude.ai storage with a real backend", Firestore, live, seeded from the 16 Nov JSON
 📦 D3: user/downloads/sample capability replacements; keep Open/Download data file
 📦 D4: "Automate the BOM weather": 6 am and afternoon job, 7 days, manual protection, refresh button, paste fallback
 📦 D5: "test one fetch of IDV10753.xml from Google Cloud and tell me" (done, works)
 📦 D6: landing page hooks OSS_USER_NAME and OSS_LOGOUT_URL
 📦 D7: hosting at nicholaswood.com.au path, vendored libs with CSP, same project/region/CI/secrets pattern, Terraform
 📦 D8: short README: deploy, rollback, rerun weather, restore

🚀 PARALLELISM OPPORTUNITIES:
 🚀 GCP project, Firestore, Firebase bootstrap (Mac gcloud, background)
 🚀 Advisor call on the approach
 🚀 Read AccessBuddy auth modules for the port
 🚀 Launch pattern: background Bash plus foreground reads now; Forge or Engineer for the app scaffold after reads

# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AccessBuddy — Continuous Integration
# ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_call:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint-and-type-check:
    name: Lint & Type Check
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint
        run: bun run lint

      - name: Type check
        run: bun run typecheck

  test:
    name: Test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: accessbuddy
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: testpassword
          POSTGRES_DB: accessbuddy_test
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd="pg_isready -U accessbuddy"
          --health-interval=10s
          --health-timeout=5s
          --health-retries=5

      redis:
        image: redis:7
        ports:
          - 6379:6379
        options: >-
          --health-cmd="redis-cli ping"
          --health-interval=10s
          --health-timeout=5s
          --health-retries=5

    env:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://accessbuddy:testpassword@localhost:5432/accessbuddy_test
      REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      # Applies ALL migrations from zero; migrate.ts's built-in post-migration
      # integrity check verifies every journal-promised table exists and exits
      # non-zero on drift (the incident class where prod's drizzle bookkeeping
      # said 0010-0012 were applied while rate_limit_buckets did not exist).
      - name: Run database migrations
        run: bun run db:migrate

      # Diffs the freshly-migrated database against the Drizzle schema
      # definitions via drizzle-kit's push planner (dry-run) — catches tables,
      # columns, and indexes declared in schema/*.ts that no migration creates.
      - name: Schema drift check (drizzle-kit diff vs migrated database)
        run: bun run db:check-drift

      - name: Run tests
        run: bun run test

  build:
    name: Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint-and-type-check, test]

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build
        run: bun run build

== advisor

## Other risks, either design

7. **Path routing.** Cloud Run domain mappings cannot route `/lsv/dailysummary`. You need either a global HTTPS load balancer with a path matcher, or a Firebase Hosting rewrite.
   - If you use Hosting, it strips every cookie except `__session`. Name the cookie `__session` or auth will silently fail.
   - Scope the cookie with `Path=/lsv`.
   - Add `nicholaswood.com.au` to Firebase Auth authorized domains for the magic-link `continueUrl`.

8. **Scheduler.**
   - Set `time_zone = "Australia/Melbourne"` so DST doesn't shift the twice-daily runs.
   - Compare the cron secret in constant time.
   - Keep the secret in Secret Manager, not tfvars (another AccessBuddy drift lesson).
   - Consider Scheduler OIDC plus an invoker-only internal path instead of the secret.

9. **BOM FTP.**
   - Test passive-mode FTP from Cloud Run egress early.
   - Make the job idempotent per observation timestamp.
   - When BOM is late or missing a value, never overwrite a manual value and never write nulls.

10. **Deploy hazards.**
    - Auto-mode may block `gcloud` and Terraform steps. Plan to hand Nick the commands.
    - Do the first WIF bind manually and import it into Terraform.

## Bottom line

Decide proxy vs direct on one question: are real-time listeners a requirement?
- If not, proxy, and items 1–6 disappear.
- If so, items 1–4 are mandatory before ship, not polish.

FROM oven/bun:1.3 AS base

FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

FROM base AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# NEXT_PUBLIC_* are inlined into the client bundle at build time (same
# pattern as AccessBuddy). Pass them with --build-arg.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
RUN bun run build

FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
RUN groupadd --system --gid 1001 nodejs && useradd --system --uid 1001 --gid nodejs nextjs
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/oss ./oss
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME="0.0.0.0"
CMD ["bun", "server.js"]

FROM oven/bun:1.3 AS base

FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

FROM base AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# NEXT_PUBLIC_* are inlined into the client bundle at build time (same
# pattern as AccessBuddy). Pass them with --build-arg.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
RUN bun run build

FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
RUN groupadd --system --gid 1001 nodejs && useradd --system --uid 1001 --gid nodejs nextjs
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/oss ./oss
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME="0.0.0.0"
CMD ["bun", "server.js"]

# Public (inlined at build)
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=lsv-oss-prod.firebaseapp.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=lsv-oss-prod
NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=

# Server
# At least 32 characters. Signs OTP sessions. Fails closed when missing.
SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET=
# Optional: when set, magic links and codes are sent through Resend from
# RESEND_FROM (a verified Resend domain). When unset, Firebase sends the
# magic link itself and the email-code sign-in is hidden.
RESEND_API_KEY=
RESEND_FROM="LSV Service Summary <noreply@example.com>"
# Service account email Cloud Scheduler uses to call /api/cron/weather (OIDC).
CRON_INVOKER_EMAIL=
# Local dev only: path to a service-account JSON. On Cloud Run ADC is used.
GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS=
# Local dev only, never in production.
ENABLE_DEV_LOGIN=false

name: Deploy

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: lsv-oss-prod
  GCP_REGION: australia-southeast1
  CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE: lsv-oss-prod
  AR_REPO: lsv-oss
  IMAGE_NAME: app

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Cloud Run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ci]
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

      - name: Build image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://nicholaswood.com.au \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=lsv-oss-prod.firebaseapp.com \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:latest .

      - name: Push image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker push ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:latest

      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} \
            --image=${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} \
            --project=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

      - name: Verify deployed version
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -fsS https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary/api/health | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q '"version":"${{ inputs.version }}"'

input.content:
# LSV Operational Service Summary

Life Saving Victoria's Operational Service Summary tool, hosted at
`https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary` behind AccessBuddy's sign-in
pattern, with Firestore for live multi-member data and a scheduled BOM
weather job.

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| GCP project | `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1 |
| Runtime | Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod` (Next.js 15, Bun image, min 0 instances) |
| Data | Firestore Native `(default)`; rules in `firestore.rules` |
| Sign-in | Firebase Auth email link (and email code when Resend is configured); 14-day httpOnly `session` cookie; member allow-list in `members/` |
| Weather | Cloud Scheduler `lsv-oss-weather-morning` 06:00 and `-afternoon` 16:30 Melbourne → `GET /api/cron/weather` (OIDC) |
| Infra | `infra/terraform` (state in `gs://lsv-oss-prod-tfstate`) |
| Deploy | GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` on every push, `release-please.yml` cuts a release and runs `deploy.yml` over Workload Identity Federation |

## The page

`oss/index.html` is the built artifact page. Edit the parts under
`oss/src/ux/` and run `python3 build.py` there to rebuild; never hand-edit the
built file. The server injects, per request, a CSP nonce on each script tag,
`window.OSS_USER_NAME`, `window.OSS_LOGOUT_URL`, `window.OSS_BOOTSTRAP`, and
`/vendor/bridge.js`, which provides `window.OSS_BACKEND` (`db`, `user`,
`downloads`, `refreshWeather`, `logout`) in place of the claude.ai
capabilities. docx, xlsx and jszip are vendored in `public/vendor` by
`bun run vendor` (hashes in `scripts/vendor.lock.json`) so the CSP is
`'self'`-only.

## Local development

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env            # fill the NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* values
gcloud auth application-default login --project lsv-oss-prod
bun run vendor && bun run dev   # http://localhost:3000/lsv/dailysummary
```

Add yourself to the allow-list once (or use the seed `--admin` flag):

```bash
bun run seed path/to/data.json --admin you@example.com "Your Name"
```

## Deploy

A deploy is a release. Merge conventional-commit PRs to `main`; release-please
opens a release PR; merging it creates the release and `deploy.yml` builds,
pushes `:sha`, `:vX.Y.Z` and `:latest` to Artifact Registry, updates the Cloud
Run service and checks `/api/health` reports the new version.

After merging a release PR, do not merge anything else to `main` until
"Deploy to Cloud Run" is green. If a later push cancels the release run,
`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed` re-runs the deploy for that release.

GitHub repository secrets (values from `terraform output`):
`GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER`, `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID`.

Manual deploy from a laptop (emergency only):

```bash
IMG=australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/lsv-oss-prod/lsv-oss/app:manual-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)
docker build --platform linux/amd64 --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://nicholaswood.com.au \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=... --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=lsv-oss-prod.firebaseapp.com \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=lsv-oss-prod --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=... -t $IMG .
docker push $IMG
gcloud run services update lsv-oss-prod --image=$IMG --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

## Rollback

Cloud Run keeps every revision. Send traffic back to the previous one:

```bash
gcloud run revisions list --service=lsv-oss-prod --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
gcloud run services update-traffic lsv-oss-prod --to-revisions=<previous-revision>=100 \
  --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

Rolling back code does not roll back data. Firestore has no schema
migrations in this app, so older revisions read current data fine.

## Infrastructure changes

```bash
cd infra/terraform
```

| Data | Firestore Native `(default)`; rules in `firestore.rules` |
| Sign-in | Firebase Auth email link (and email code when Resend is configured); 14-day httpOnly `session` cookie; member allow-list in `members/` |
| Weather | Cloud Scheduler `lsv-oss-weather-morning` 06:00 and `-afternoon` 16:30 Melbourne → `GET /api/cron/weather` (OIDC) |
| Infra | `infra/terraform` (state in `gs://lsv-oss-prod-tfstate`) |
| Deploy | GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` on every push, `release-please.yml` cuts a release and runs `deploy.yml` over Workload Identity Federation |

`oss/src/ux/` and run `python3 build.py` there to rebuild; never hand-edit the

`window.OSS_USER_NAME`, `window.OSS_LOGOUT_URL`, `window.OSS_BOOTSTRAP`, and
`/vendor/bridge.js`, which provides `window.OSS_BACKEND` (`db`, `user`,
`downloads`, `refreshWeather`, `logout`) in place of the claude.ai
capabilities. docx, xlsx and jszip are vendored in `public/vendor` by
`bun run vendor` (hashes in `scripts/vendor.lock.json`) so the CSP is

Rolling back code does not roll back data. Firestore has no schema
migrations in this app, so older revisions read current data fine.

## Infrastructure changes

```bash
cd infra/terraform
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=lsv-oss-prod-tfstate"
terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars
terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
```

`prod.tfvars` is gitignored. Firestore rules deploy with Terraform
(`google_firebaserules_release`), so a rules change is a Terraform apply.

Domain: Cloud Run domain mapping on `nicholaswood.com.au` (Google-managed
TLS). One-off steps the account owner does: verify the domain
(`gcloud domains verify nicholaswood.com.au`), create the mapping
(`gcloud beta run domain-mappings create --service lsv-oss-prod --domain nicholaswood.com.au --region australia-southeast1`),
copy the A/AAAA records it prints into `cloud_run_domain_ipv4/6` in
`prod.tfvars`, apply, and point GoDaddy's nameservers at the Cloud DNS
`dns_name_servers` output.

## Weather job

Runs 06:00 and 16:30 Melbourne via Cloud Scheduler. It fetches
`IDV10753.xml`, `IDV10752.xml` and `IDV10751.xml` over the BOM's anonymous FTP,
projects towns onto areas (`src/lib/weather/mapping.ts`, the server twin of the
page's `BOM_FEED`), and writes `weather/<YYYY-MM-DD>` for seven days with
`source: "BOM forecast issued <time>"`. Cells listed in a day's `manual` array
(`"<area>|<field>"`) were typed by a member and are never overwritten. Status
is in `config/weatherStatus` (last run, last issued, last error).

Rerun it:

```bash
# From the UI: Weather tab → Refresh from BOM now (session-gated, 2/min).
# From Scheduler:
gcloud scheduler jobs run lsv-oss-weather-morning --location=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
# From a laptop with ADC:
bun run weather            # writes
bun run weather --dry-run  # prints the grid, no writes
```

Logs: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND textPayload:"[weather]"' --project=lsv-oss-prod --limit=20`.

BOM licence: anonymous FTP data is for internal organisational use. The site
stays behind sign-in; nothing from the feeds is served to anonymous requests.

## Backup and restore

Members: Settings → Download data file produces
`{ format: "lsv-operational-service-summary", docs: {...} }`; Settings → Open
data file writes it back through the signed-in session.

Ops restore from a file (idempotent; `--replace` also deletes docs not in the file):

```bash
bun run seed "Operational Service Summary data 2026-11-16.json"
bun run seed backup.json --replace
```

Point-in-time export for safekeeping:

```bash
gcloud firestore export gs://lsv-oss-prod-tfstate/firestore-export/$(date +%F) --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

## Members

Allow-list docs live in `members/<email>` with `displayName` and `role`
(`member` or `admin`). Add or change via the API as an admin:

```bash
curl -X PUT https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary/api/members \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -b 'session=...' \
  -d '{"email":"person@lsv.com.au","displayName":"First Last","role":"member"}'
```

or with the seed script's `--admin` flag for the first admin. Removing a member
revokes their Firebase refresh tokens, so open tabs lose data access within an
hour and the next page load is refused.

## Rules

- Never call LIMSOC production. Unit data came from staging only.
- Wording: members, not staff. `unit.area` is Region (Central/East/West);
  `unit.regionName` is Area (Bass, Port Phillip, Kingston, ...).
- Costs: everything here sits in GCP free tiers except the Cloud DNS zone
  (about US$0.20 a month). No Cloud SQL, no load balancer, min instances 0.

- 2026-11-16T10:48Z — **Nick's decisions:** Firestore for data, host `nicholaswood.com.au`, new GCP project. CSP explained; default is vendored libraries plus strict CSP unless he objects. Pack reported dropped but still not found on Linux, Mac, OneDrive or the harness download folders after a fresh rescan; asked where.
- 2026-11-16T10:58Z — **FirstPrinciples on access control.** The session cookie and the Firestore token are the same Firebase identity. Design: membership is enforced server-side (`/api/auth/session` checks the `members/` allow-list before issuing the cookie, exactly where AccessBuddy checks memberships), then custom claims `member`/`admin` are set on the Firebase user; the browser Firestore SDK authenticates with the member's own Firebase session, or, when the browser has none (OTP path, cleared site data), with a custom token minted at `POST /api/auth/firebase-token` behind the cookie. Rules require the claim and validate `updatedBy == uid`, `updatedAt == request.time`, known collections, size. Rejected: proxying Firestore through Cloud Run over SSE, because long-lived streams are billed CPU time and would break the free-tier expectation under open tabs.
- 2026-11-16T11:05Z — **Advisor (Inference.ts) consulted before build.** Adopted: rules shape checks with `updatedBy`/`updatedAt`, POST-only Origin-checked no-store mint endpoint, CSP connect-src for the three Google hosts, Scheduler OIDC instead of a shared header, `time_zone = Australia/Melbourne`, idempotent job, never write nulls. Noted: Cloud Run domain mappings cannot route by path, so the mapping owns the whole host and Next.js `basePath` serves `/lsv/dailysummary`; the apex is free for a later personal site only via Firebase Hosting rewrites (cookie would need renaming to `__session`), recorded as a future option, not done.
- 2026-11-16T11:06Z — **Scheduler auth is OIDC, not `x-cron-secret`.** Deviation from AccessBuddy on advisor advice: the route verifies a Google-signed ID token for the scheduler service account and audience; no secret in Terraform state or job definition. # Projects

> Index of Nick's active projects. Loaded at session start via CLAUDE.md `@` import. Each entry links to its detail file. The DA uses this to know what Nick is working on and how to approach each.

## Career & Consulting

- **[Virgin Australia](~/Documents/workspace/projects/virgin-australia/README.md)** - Nick's role: Senior AI Engineer, CIO/AI team, Brisbane (started ~Aug 2026). First initiative: TA + onboarding AI discovery interrogating the BCG savings recommendation. Discovery approach at `projects/virgin-australia/talent-acquisition/DiscoveryApproach.md`; initiative ISA alongside it.
- **[Career Pivot](career-pivot.md)** - Engineering to digital strategy consulting. Resolved for now: joined Virgin Australia as Senior AI Engineer (Aug 2026). Consulting entity and case studies retained as options.
- **[LIMSOC National IMS](limsoc-national-ims.md)** - **Completed (2026).** Paid SLSA consulting engagement: national IMS architecture, governance, commercials, rollout. Now the lead case study for the consulting pivot.

## Products (SaaS)

- **[AccessBuddy](accessbuddy.md)** - Multi-tenant club access & credential management SaaS. Live at accessbuddy.com.au (v1.10.2); SMLSC is first tenant (192 members, 354 credentials). Next.js + Bun + Hono + Postgres + GCP. _SaaS pricing / second-club GTM still open._
- **[LifesaverOnCall](lifesaveroncall.md)** - GoodSAM-style emergency dispatch product for LSV. Pre-launch; Phase 3 complete, Phase 4 blockers open.

## Surf Lifesaving

- **[LSV Communications Officer](lsv-comms-officer.md)** - Nick's volunteer State Lifesaving Communications Officer role at Life Saving Victoria. Scope: LIMSOC, Operational Communications, LSOCE.
- **[SMLSC Club](club-renewal.md)** - South Melbourne Lifesaving Club. Master plan across area codes, VESEP funding model, board proposal.

## Personal

- **[Personal](personal.md)** - Gym / strength training, Hazel dog co-ownership, spare room rental, EV decision, home automation. (The former `life` project was retired 2026-06-02: its threads live here; its orchestration cadence is now a DA rhythm - see `Routines/weekly-review.md`.)
- **[BYD Shark 6 Performance](byd-shark-6.md)** - Buy-and-build decision for a BYD Shark 6 Performance PHEV ute (touring fitout: RAID bull bar, glass canopy, roof racks, drawers, fridge). Payload worked out 2026-06-25: factory 725 kg (GVM 3,500 − kerb 2,775), ~460 kg remaining after ~265 kg of accessories/fitout. **Resolved:** run as-is now, GVM upgrade deferrable; weighbridge the built rig axle-by-axle, and note a later GVM upgrade costs more than a pre-rego one. Detail at `projects/byd-shark-6/README.md`.
- **[OC EV / Energy Tender](~/Documents/workspace/projects/oc-ev-energy/README.md)** - Owners Corporation decision project for 40-44 Pakington St, St Kilda (OC 728653T). Two proposals: Origin EV backbone ($125k, OC-owned, no lock-in) vs SUPA embedded-network energy deal ($0 upfront, 10yr+ supply lock-in, 3 chargers as sweetener). They are NOT like-for-like. Committee reply-all sent 2026-06-24 (positions the two as non-equivalent, requests written terms from both providers, floats a SUPA intercom add-on, proposes a meeting once both reply). Awaiting SUPA term-sheet + Origin firm quote/ownership confirmation. Foundation collated at `projects/oc-ev-energy/FOUNDATION.md`.

## Systems / Tooling

- **[Life OS Console](life-os-console.md)** - Local agent-operations cockpit: a Discord/Slack bot surfacing the workspace agents as a chat roster, routing through the PAI inference pipeline with approval gates.
- **[PAI workspace tooling](pai.md)** - The hand-rolled workspace life-OS (AGENT_STANDARD, agent-onboarder, maintainer, OneDrive convention). Converging into the live PAI 5.x system.

---

## Convergence status (2026-06-02)

All 10 projects converged onto PAI conventions: each has a twelve-section `<project>/ISA.md` in its repo (the system of record), specialist agents registered as PAI subagents with distinct voices and tool-scoping, and a KNOWLEDGE note indexed for retrieval. Recipe: `_CONVERGENCE_RECIPE.md`. Files stay in `~/Documents/workspace/`; only this index, the agent registry, and the knowledge index live under `~/.claude/PAI`.

## Open Sessions to Resume

- **Helm trading engine** (built 2026-09-12/13, deployed in paper mode): `~/Documents/workspace/projects/helm`, ISA at `helm/ISA.md`, runbook `helm/RUNBOOK.md`. Daily paper timer 16:30 Sydney and watchdog 18:30 installed. Replay 2026-06-10..09-10 showed both strategies below the STW benchmark with costs dominating; rank hysteresis and weekly rebalance added. Gated on Nick reading the Virgin Australia securities trading policy, choosing ASX (IBKR) or US microcaps (Alpaca plus FMP keys in .env), and a 2 to 4 week forward paper record before approve mode. Next step if resumed: review reports/replay.html, decide asset class, fund keys.

- **Inkwell / PAI Task System** (parked 2026-06-18): personal task system to replace Nick's paper notebook, built on PAI. Name committed (Inkwell). State persisted at `~/Documents/workspace/projects/inkwell/STATE.md` — pre-build, pre-ISA. Build is gated on five answers Nick must give (L1 capture device, L3 store, L4 agent autonomy, L8 bake-off metric, A4 ISA-relationship); STATE.md records my recommended position on each plus defaults for the deferred eight. Next step when resumed: Nick answers the five, then I write the E3 twelve-section ISA at `projects/inkwell/ISA.md` and delegate the MVP (CLI + SQLite + Telegram capture + 17:00 check-in) to a feature-dev subagent. Source docs in `PAI/MEMORY/WORK/pai-task-system/`. Not yet registered in the Products/Systems index above.
- **BudgetBuddy / envelope-os build** (parked 2026-06-29; renamed from Penny): zero-based envelope budgeting on direct Australian bank feeds via Basiq (CDR), feeding Pulse. Project at `~/Documents/workspace/projects/envelope-os/`; project ISA now 128 ISCs (extended 2026-06-29 with the Basiq migration, ISC-105..128). **Provider pivot decided:** dropping PocketSmith for direct Basiq feeds because PocketSmith is a paid per-user dependency and a bridge that blocks a future multi-user product; BudgetBuddy is already multi-tenant (Store scoped by userId), so PocketSmith was the only structural blocker. Design written at `docs/BASIQ_MIGRATION_SPEC.md` (IngestProvider port, BasiqProvider with CDR consent flow + job-poll, owned categorisation layer replacing PocketSmith's category tree; secret model inverted to one app-level Basiq key + in-app consent). Build scope: single-user (Nick) now, product-shaped; multi-user CDR-representative onboarding deferred. **Next step when resumed: BUILD** the IngestProvider port + BasiqProvider + Categoriser, verifying the confirm-in-sandbox items (token scopes, consent handoff, job steps, transaction field names/sign) against the Basiq sandbox. **External prereq (owner: Nick):** free Basiq developer account at dashboard.basiq.io for sandbox API keys — the only external blocker to starting BUILD; production CDR onboarding (paid, per-connection) deferred to multi-user. Prior provisional flags (rollover deficit-booking, every-dollar at wizard completion) still carried as working defaults. Not yet registered in the Products/Systems index above.
- **Programmatic resume export pipeline** (deferred 2026-06-12, from Virgin application thread): markdown → template-faithful `.docx` automation. Attempted: bun `docx` package (wrong styling), then pandoc `--reference-doc` + a transformer script (close, but final fidelity rejected). Decision: manual Word export for now; CLAUDE.md's "python-docx, no manual export" clause is aspirational until this is built (python-docx NOT installed; no pip on the Linux box). If resumed: install a docx toolchain, rebuild the transformer in `PAI/TOOLS/`, end the pipeline with explicit `rclone copy` push (mount uploads stall silently).
- **LinkedIn recruiter reply — Senior Platform Engineer** (on hold per Nick 2026-06-11): draft reply template exists (peer-tone thanks + comp/hybrid/AI-focus/team-size questions); needs recruiter name, company, role link, and original message text before finalising.

FROM oven/bun:1.3 AS base

FROM base AS deps
WORKDIR /app
COPY package.json bun.lock ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile

FROM base AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
# NEXT_PUBLIC_* are inlined into the client bundle at build time (same
# pattern as AccessBuddy). Pass them with --build-arg.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=$NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID
RUN bun run build

FROM base AS runner
WORKDIR /app
ENV NODE_ENV=production
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1
RUN groupadd --system --gid 1001 nodejs && useradd --system --uid 1001 --gid nodejs nextjs
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/oss ./oss
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
ENV PORT=3000
ENV HOSTNAME="0.0.0.0"
CMD ["bun", "server.js"]
